calibration.reason: Clear labels and a legible familiar layout support the task, while misplaced focus after invalid input makes recovery harder.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight.
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected, focus remained visible, and the path, ferry and footbridge appeared in the result.

A-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; the result list contained only Riverside path closes.
A-1440.fact_check: At 6 m the water surface aligns with the illustrated 6 m marker and the text says 6 m. The displayed thresholds and closures are internally consistent; their real-world accuracy is unsupported.
A-1440.strength: The large illustrated river and compact result make the selected level easy to connect to its consequences.
A-1440.weakness: The illustration shows a ferry at the waterline even when the result says ferry stops, leaving its operational state visually ambiguous.
A-1440.repair: Give stopped crossings a clear visual treatment or label in the illustration.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected and all three closures appeared. The result, illustration and threshold legend were readable within the 390 × 844 initial viewport.

A-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; only Riverside path closes remained in the result list.
A-390.fact_check: The water surface aligns with the 6 m marker and the displayed value. Actual local closure thresholds are unsupported by a cited source.
A-390.strength: The controls and complete result fit comfortably above the illustration, with visible keyboard focus.
A-390.weakness: The small ferry and bridge details make their changed states less apparent on mobile.
A-390.repair: Add compact state cues to the illustration while keeping the result visible above the fold.

primary_action.input: Tab to the slider, then Tab through the closure rows to the 6 m footbridge row and press Space. Two initial ArrowRight presses on the slider moved it from 4 to 4.2 m.
primary_action.expected: Jump to 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: The row action set 6 m; the path and footbridge showed Closed and the ferry showed Stopped.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two Shift+Tab presses and Space on the 2 m row set 2 m. Only the path was marked closed; ferry and footbridge remained listed as Level not reached.
B-1440.fact_check: The waterline aligns with the 6 m scale and the text reads 6 m. The ferry remains drawn at the 4 m height, submerged beneath the 6 m waterline. Real-world thresholds are unsupported by a cited source.
B-1440.strength: The cross-section and explicit reached versus not-reached statuses explain the thresholds clearly.
B-1440.weakness: The submerged ferry conflicts with the physical scene, and the closure rows' direct-set behavior is not obvious visually.
B-1440.repair: Keep the ferry floating at the current waterline and visibly indicate that each threshold row sets the level.

primary_action.input: Tab through the slider and closure rows to the 6 m footbridge row, then press Space.
primary_action.expected: Jump to 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: The level changed to 6 m and all three rows showed closed or stopped. The complete result was readable within the 390 × 844 viewport.

B-390.edge_observation: Two Shift+Tab presses and Space set 2 m. The path alone was marked closed; the other two rows remained visible as Level not reached.
B-390.fact_check: The waterline reaches the 6 m mark and matches the text, but the ferry is drawn underwater. Actual local closure thresholds are unsupported by a cited source.
B-390.strength: The cross-section, level and all three status rows fit in the first mobile viewport.
B-390.weakness: The diagram's labels are small, and the row controls look like static status rows until focused.
B-390.repair: Increase diagram label legibility and add a visible affordance for setting a threshold.

preference.reason: A makes the requested jump and resulting closures immediately clear with prominent level choices, visible focus and a compact mobile result. B's cross-section is informative, but its ferry appears submerged at 6 m and its threshold-row actions are less discoverable.

decision: The tighter floodwall improved within its series. Round 5 remains the best. Draw a clearer stopped-state marker where the ferry still floats.
